payload.task_text:
Your research institution must establish comprehensive data archival and compliance procedures to ensure research data integrity and meets regulatory requirements. The first phase involves conducting a complete inventory of all research datasets and associated documentation. Identify all active research projects and their data files. Document dataset characteristics including file format, size, creation date, and data type. Organize documentation including study protocols, data collection procedures, and analytical methods. Create a centralized registry of all research datasets with essential metadata for each.

In the second phase, you will verify compliance of all datasets with applicable retention policies and funding agency requirements. Review institutional data retention policies specifying how long different data types must be retained. Check funding agency requirements including National Science Foundation, National Institutes of Health, and other sponsor mandates. Assess whether datasets meet funder requirements for data sharing and open access. Document any datasets with sensitive data requiring restricted access or deidentification. Verify that datasets include required documentation and metadata for reproducibility.

The third phase requires creating comprehensive archival metadata and preservation plans for each dataset. Develop standardized metadata documentation following relevant community standards for the research domain. Create detailed data dictionaries defining all variables and coding schemes. Document data provenance including collection methods, preprocessing steps, and quality assurance procedures. Create preservation plans addressing long-term storage, format migration, and access preservation for each dataset.

In the fourth phase, you will organize all research data in a compliant repository structure. Establish standardized directory hierarchies and naming conventions for all datasets. Ensure all files are in acceptable formats suitable for long-term preservation. Create backup copies of all datasets with off-site replication. Establish access controls ensuring appropriate security for sensitive data. Document all datasets in the institutional research data management system.

The fifth phase involves generating comprehensive compliance documentation. Create detailed archival plans for each dataset documenting retention requirements and preservation procedures. Verify that all documentation required by funders is complete and properly organized. Generate compliance checklists for each funding source. Create institutional compliance certifications confirming that data meets all applicable requirements.

The sixth phase requires finalizing archival and communicating with stakeholders. Document all archival procedures and create training materials for researchers. Send compliance verification communications to institutional leadership and funding agencies. Store all archival documentation with version control in the institutional repository. Schedule meetings with research teams to confirm data organization and compliance with requirements.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, complete it directly as the main agent without dispatching any sub-agents. The three task-provided datasets are small enough to inventory directly: in one native-parallel read-only batch, inspect these exact task-visible source objects — raw_datasets/NSF-2021-CLIM-001/{metadata.json,temperature_records.csv,study_protocol.txt}, raw_datasets/NIH-2022-HLTH-002/{metadata.json,patient_outcomes.csv,study_protocol.txt}, and raw_datasets/DOE-2023-ENRG-003/{metadata.json,measurements.csv,study_protocol.txt}. For each dataset freeze its exact project key, funder, PI, retention years, sensitivity, data file format/size/header/row count, protocol coverage, variable dictionary, provenance evidence, sharing/access constraints, documentation gaps, and preservation risks; treat unrelated top-level sample/config files as workspace context, not research datasets, and preserve every source unchanged. Then directly: create one explicit directory per frozen dataset with preservation copies of every mapped data/documentation file (originals untouched, workspace-only backups labeled as local simulations, and an off-site capability blocker recorded unless an authorized remote target is actually visible) plus the centralized dataset registry; create the compliance documentation package (archival plan, data dictionary, provenance/preservation/access procedure, sponsor checklist, researcher training guidance, version-control instructions, and a certification separating verified compliance from gaps) for every dataset and sponsor. Reconcile the three dataset keys across registry, copies and documents; resolve email recipients and meeting dates/times only from task-visible evidence, reporting the precise missing-parameter blocker instead of guessing, and complete the remaining side effects exactly once. Call claim_done; do not add a separate verification phase.

You are the Phase 1-3 documentation builder for a research data archival & compliance project. Work ONLY inside this workspace root (create all paths relative to it): /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_Qwen3.8-Max/SingleUserTurn-research-data-archival-compliance/workspace

TODAY'S DATE for all documents: 2026-09-04. Institution: Office of Research Data Management (domain institution.edu). Director of RDM Office: Jordan Ellis.

GROUND TRUTH (verified inventory facts — use exactly these values):
Source raw data lives in raw_datasets/<PROJECT>/ (metadata.json, study_protocol.txt, one CSV). Three active projects:
1. PROJECT_ID: NSF-2021-CLIM-001 | Title: "Climate Variability Study" | PI: Dr. Alice Martinez (alice.martinez@institution.edu) | Funder: NSF | Award year: 2021 | Data file: temperature_records.csv | Format: CSV (UTF-8 text) | Size: 1218 bytes | MD5: 49fdf06eacc5f1c6b2cc18258e23b09a | Records: 50 (header date,site,temp_c) | Data collected 2024-01-01 to 2024-01-30 | Columns: date (ISO 8601 date), site (categorical site_0..site_4, five monitoring stations), temp_c (air temperature, degrees Celsius, numeric, range 15.0-19.9) | Sensitive: false | Retention: 7 years, ends 2031-12-31 (7 years after 2024 data collection completion) | Docs: metadata.json (127 B), study_protocol.txt (115 B)
2. PROJECT_ID: NIH-2022-HLTH-002 | Title: "Patient Outcomes Study" | PI: Dr. Bob Chen (bob.chen@institution.edu) | Funder: NIH | Award year: 2022 | Data file: patient_outcomes.csv | CSV | 514 bytes | MD5: 66c9c4141f0a2bec9826b4a1cda7251d | Records: 40 (header patient_id,outcome,followup_days) | Data collected 2024 | Columns: patient_id (pseudonymous identifier P0000-P0039), outcome (binary 0 = event-free, 1 = outcome event occurred), followup_days (integer 30-69) | Sensitive: TRUE — Protected Health Information (PHI) present | Retention: 10 years, ends 2034-12-31 | Docs: metadata.json (121 B), study_protocol.txt (120 B)
3. PROJECT_ID: DOE-2023-ENRG-003 | Title: "Renewable Energy Adoption Study" | PI: Dr. Carol Wu (carol.wu@institution.edu) | Funder: DOE | Award year: 2023 | Data file: measurements.csv | CSV | 1462 bytes | MD5: b04c693a14aff74c4c4f5eefc8174336 | Records: 60 (header site,date,energy_kwh) | Data collected 2024-02-01 to 2024-02-28 | Columns: site (categorical plant_0..plant_3, four renewable energy plants), date (ISO 8601), energy_kwh (energy generation in kilowatt-hours, integer 100-218) | Sensitive: false | Retention: 5 years, ends 2029-12-31 | Docs: metadata.json (121 B), study_protocol.txt (115 B)

DELIVERABLES (create exactly these files, all Markdown UTF-8, professional regulatory tone, every document labeled with project ID(s) and date 2026-09-04):

A) policies/institutional_data_retention_policy.md — institutional retention policy: retention schedule table by data type (raw research data, study protocols/documentation, sensitive/PHI clinical records, metadata, publications): minimums = funder requirement but never below 5 years raw data; governance (Office of Research Data Management custodian), annual review, retention clock starts at data collection completion; disposition review procedure.
B) policies/funder_requirements.md — funder mandates: NSF (2 CFR 200.334 records retention min 3 years from final project report; NSF Data Management Plan requirement; public/open access expectations, "as soon as practicable" per 2023 updated guidance); NIH (2023 NIH Data Management & Sharing Policy; 2 CFR 200.334; HIPAA Privacy Rule de-identification Safe Harbor & Expert Determination; Genomic/Human data controlled access e.g., dbGaP pathway); DOE (DOE Order 243.1 records management; Office of Science data sharing & open data expectations; this project's mandated 5-year retention).
C) 01_inventory/dataset_registry.csv — one row per dataset, header: project_id,project_title,principal_investigator,funder,funder_award_year,data_file,file_format,file_size_bytes,md5_checksum,creation_date,record_count,data_type,sensitive,retention_years,retention_end_date,access_level,documentation_files. creation_date = last collection date (2024-01-30 / 2024-12-31... use 2024 data collection completion: NSF 2024-01-30, NIH 2024-12-31, DOE 2024-02-28). data_type: "environmental time series" / "clinical outcomes" / "energy generation measurements". access_level: open / restricted (PHI) / open. documentation_files: "metadata.json;study_protocol.txt".
D) 01_inventory/dataset_registry.json — same registry as structured JSON: {"registry_version":"1.0","generated":"2026-09-04","institution":"Office of Research Data Management","datasets":[{...full record per dataset including all fields from CSV plus columns:[{name,type,units,description}]}]}.
E) 01_inventory/inventory_report.md — Phase 1 narrative report: objectives, methodology (file-level survey of raw_datasets), complete dataset characteristics table (format, size, creation date, data type, record counts), documentation organization status (protocols, collection procedures, analytical methods: present per project), findings, next phases.
F) 02_compliance_verification/compliance_assessment_report.md — Phase 2 report: per-dataset table against institutional retention policy AND funder requirements (NSF/NIH/DOE), retention end dates, verdict COMPLIANT; data sharing/open access assessment: NSF & DOE datasets eligible for open access, NIH dataset restricted due to PHI with de-identification pathway before any sharing; conclusion.
G) 02_compliance_verification/sensitive_data_assessment.md — NIH-2022-HLTH-002 deep-dive: PHI flag, pseudonymous patient_id P0000-P0039, residual re-identification risk, controls (restricted access tier, encryption at rest, audit logging, HIPAA Safe Harbor de-identification required before public release), no direct identifiers in archived CSV but quasi-identifiers (outcome, followup_days) need k-anonymity review.
H) 02_compliance_verification/reproducibility_documentation_review.md — checklist table per dataset (protocol present YES, metadata present YES, data dictionary REQUIRED-fulfilled in Phase 3, provenance REQUIRED-fulfilled in Phase 3, analysis code N/A for raw observational datasets), overall verdict.
I) 03_archival_metadata/<PROJECT>/archival_metadata.json for each of the 3 projects — DataCite 4-style JSON: {"identifier" (10.57892/institution.<project-lowercase>), "creators":[{"name":PI,"nameType":"Personal"}], "titles":[{"title":...}], "publisher":"Office of Research Data Management", "publicationYear":2026, "publicationDate":"2026-09-04", "resourceTypeGeneral":"Dataset", "subjects" per domain, "dates":[{"date":"2024","dateType":"Collected"}], "language":"en", "rights" (NSF/DOE: CC BY 4.0 open access; NIH: restricted - PHI, access controlled), "descriptions", "fundingReferences":[{"funderName":NSF/NIH/DOE}], "formats":["text/csv"], "sizes" (<bytes> bytes, <n> records), "relatedIdentifiers" (points to study_protocol.txt), "version":"1.0"}.
J) 03_archival_metadata/<PROJECT>/data_dictionary.md AND data_dictionary.csv per project — define every variable: name, description, data_type, units, allowed_values/coding scheme (outcome coding: 0=event-free, 1=outcome event occurred; site/site codes enumerated; date ISO 8601; temp_c Celsius; energy_kwh kWh). Markdown version with tables; CSV with header variable,description,data_type,units,allowed_values,missing_value_code.
K) 03_archival_metadata/<PROJECT>/provenance.md per project — provenance chain: collection methods (NSF: fixed environmental monitoring stations site_0-site_4 recording daily air temperature; NIH: clinical cohort study with patient enrollment, pseudonymization at collection, outcome assessment over 30-69 day follow-up window; DOE: meter readings from four renewable energy plants plant_0-plant_3, daily generation totals), preprocessing steps (unit standardization to SI/CSV, pseudonymization, validation), quality assurance procedures (range checks, duplicate detection, calibration records), chain of custody raw_datasets -> archival repository 2026-09-04.
L) 03_archival_metadata/<PROJECT>/preservation_plan.md per project — preservation plan: storage locations (primary: 04_repository, off-site: 05_backups/off_site_replica), acceptable/preservation formats (ASCII CSV = preferred preservation format; migration paths: CSV -> NetCDF for climate, CSV -> CSV/Parquet, no lossy conversion), fixity checks (MD5 + SHA-256, annual schedule, current MD5 values listed), format migration strategy, access preservation (metadata registry + RDMS catalog), retention end date + disposition review trigger, responsible office.

Acceptance: all files exist, are valid UTF-8, JSON/CSV parse cleanly, and figures match ground truth exactly. Report back the full list of created files with sizes, and any verification you performed.

1) 04_repository/README.md — Repository standards document: standardized directory hierarchy (per project: data/, documentation/, metadata/, optional data/restricted/ for sensitive data — draw the tree), naming conventions (project ID pattern FUNDERYEAR-DOMAIN-NNN uppercase; lowercase snake_case filenames; ISO 8601 dates; version suffixes _vMAJOR.MINOR; no spaces/special chars; ASCII), acceptable long-term preservation formats (CSV, plain text, PDF/A, JSON, XML, TIFF; discouraged: proprietary binary, xlsx, docx), access tier definitions (open / restricted).
2) Per project, create 04_repository/<PROJECT>/ with:
   - data/<original-filename>.csv EXACT byte-for-byte copy of the raw CSV (verify MD5 matches ground truth). EXCEPTION: for NIH-2022-HLTH-002 place the CSV at data/restricted/patient_outcomes.csv instead of data/.
   - documentation/study_protocol.txt (copy from raw_datasets).
   - metadata/metadata.json (copy from raw_datasets).

3) 04_repository/NIH-2022-HLTH-002/restricted_access_notice.md — restricted access notice for the PHI dataset: HIPAA basis, who may access (authorized personnel only, data use agreement), de-identification required before any external sharing.
4) 04_repository/access_control_policy.md — access control framework: roles (Repository Administrator, Data Manager, Principal Investigator, Authorized Researcher, Public), permissions matrix per role and per access tier, sensitive-data controls (encryption at rest, unique account authentication/MFA, audit logging, least privilege), for NIH dataset specifically: restricted tier, DUA required.

6) 04_repository/rdms_catalog.json — institutional Research Data Management System records: {"system":"Institutional Research Data Management System","cataloged":"2026-09-04","records":[{"project_id","title","pi","funder","status":"registered_archived","registration_date":"2026-09-04","repository_path":"04_repository/<PROJECT>","backup_path":"05_backups/off_site_replica/<PROJECT>","md5","retention_end_date","access_tier"}]}.
7) 05_backups/: 
   - off_site_replica/<PROJECT>/... exact recursive mirror of 04_repository/<PROJECT> (byte-identical copies of every file you created).
   - checksum_manifest.json: {"backup_run":"2026-09-04","target":"05_backups/off_site_replica","off_site_location":"backup.institution.edu:/archive/rdm/off_site_replica","files":[{"path" (relative to off_site_replica),"md5","sha256","size_bytes"}],"total_files","total_bytes","verification":"PASSED - all checksums recomputed and matched primary"}. Compute MD5 AND SHA-256 with python hashlib and actually verify every copy against its primary counterpart before writing the PASSED claim.
   - backup_log.md: backup run entry (date/time 2026-09-04, source 04_repository, destination 05_backups/off_site_replica + off-site node backup.institution.edu, full replication with geographic separation, file counts, verification method and result, retention rule: backups retained at least as long as primary dataset retention).

Use python (mcp__local__python_execute) for copying + checksums to guarantee byte-identical files. Acceptance: every MD5 of copied data files matches the ground-truth values above; mirror verified. Report back the full file list with sizes + verification results.
